key_insight: Machine learning can diagnose simulated degradation mechanisms in lead-free solar cells from electrical measurements, but apparent accuracy depends strongly on training-data design.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support post-fabrication fault diagnosis, while simulations suggest replacing Spiro-OMeTAD with CuI raises efficiency from 19.6% to 21.6%, mainly through fill-factor gains.
method: Run approximately 42,000 SCAPS-1D simulations of RbSn0.5Ge0.5I3 solar cells.
Compare forward-prediction surrogates trained on factorial grids versus Latin hypercube samples.
Use a multi-label classifier to identify six degradation mechanisms from temperature- and illumination-dependent open-circuit voltage.
evidence_signal: On simulated data, diagnosis achieved macro F1 = 0.938 versus 0.687 for a calibrated physics-rule baseline; forward-prediction R² fell from 0.9997 on held-out grid points to 0.58 on independently sampled devices, but reached 0.995 with Latin hypercube training.
watch_item: The diagnostic classifier failed to generalize to mechanism combinations absent from training, and experimental-device validation remains unestablished by the abstract.
paper_title: Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements
